newsitem.title: USA: Mixed weather for U.S. cotton producer states.
newsitem.headline: Mixed weather for U.S. cotton producer states.

text.p: Scattered showers, hail, and wind stoms hit some U.S. cotton producer states this week, while others saw hot, dry conditions help promote development of crops and increase fieldwork, according to reports from the National Agricultural Statistics Service. Insect reports from most states have remained light, although growers continue to spray fields. MISSISSIPPI - According to the Mississippi Agricultural Statistics Service, there were 5.0 days suitable for fieldwork for the week ending August 3, 1997. Soil moisture conditions were rated 35 percent surplus, 46 percent adequate, 13 percent short, and six percent very short. Cotton is blooming, according to county extension officials, though still 3-4 weeks behind schedule. Cotton farmers are anxious for boll weevil eradication to start.

Cotton squaring was rated 100 percent this week versus 97 percent last week, 100 percent last year, and 100 percent on a five year average. Setting bolls rated 95 percent this week versus 84 percent last week, 100 percent last year and 94 percent on average. Crop conditions were rated eight percent excellent, 60 percent good, 22 percent fair, seven percent poor and three percent very poor.

LOUISIANA - According to Louisiana state reports, there were 5.1 days suitable for fieldwork last week. Soil moisture conditions rated 16 percent surplus, 52 percent adequate, 25 percent short, and seven percent very short. Crop conditions rated seven percent excellent, 42 percent good, 37 percent fair, 12 percent poor, and two percent very poor. Setting bolls rated 96 percent this week versus 100 percent last year and 98 percent for the five year average. There were no bolls open yet compared to one percent open at this time last year, and one percent for the average.
According to county officials, irrigation was active this week and pressure from weevils continued. Growers were actively treating fields for insects.

GEORGIA - Another week of scattered showers fell over much of the state improving soil moisture levels and crop conditions, according to the Georgia Agricultural Statistics Service. Officials reported 4.8 days suitable for fieldwork during the week. Cotton conditions are virtually unchanged from last week.

In the central part of the state, showers helped to improve cotton fields suffering from dry weather. Spraying for worms was active in the southern part of the State and pressure was increasing in many other areas. Cotton development is several days behind normal.

Soil moisture rated 19 percent surplus, 67 percent adequate, 12 percent short, and two percent very short. Crop squaring rated 99 percent versus 97 percent last week, 100 percent last year, and 100 percent for the five year average. Setting bolls rated 90 percent this week versus 80 percent last week, 97 percent last year and 95 percent on average. Crop conditions rated 14 percent excellent, 52 percent good, 30 percent fair, and four percent poor.

TEXAS - The High Plains crop continued to enjoy the hot temperatures, however some dryland fields were beginning to stress from a lack of sufficient moisture. Bolls are setting in most areas. Bolls were beginning to open in scattered fields in North Central and Blackland areas.
Harvest operations were increasing slowly in the Coastal Bend and Rio Grande Valley. Statewide cotton condition was rated at 74 percent of normal compared with 65 percent last year.

Crop conditions rated 11 percent excellent, 42 percent good, 35 percent fair, ten percent poor and two percent very poor. Squaring was rated at 99 percent versus 96 percent last week, 96 percent last year and 92 percent for the five year average. Setting bolls rated 71 percent this week versus 52 percent last week, 70 percent last year, and 60 percent on average. Bolls opening rated seven percent this week versus five percent last week, 14 percent last year and 11 percent on average.
One percent of the cotton crop is harvested according to state reports. This compares with three percent last year and three percent on a five year average.

CALIFORNIA - Field activities progressed normally under favorable conditions in most areas of the state, according to the California Agricultural Statistics Service. Cotton was blooming and setting bolls in the San Joaquin and Sacramento valleys. Cotton growers were actively spraying for aphids, lygus, mites, whiteflies, worms, and weeds.
ARIZONA - Cotton is progressing well. Latest reports indicate that crop conditions changed little from last week. Current ratings are 20 percent excellent, 59 percent good, and 19 percent fair.

Although strong storms with high winds and hail, moved through Pima and Pinal counties over the weekend, there were no reports of any significant crop damage. In the eastern counties, heat stress is building with higher humidity brought on by monsoon conditions. Approximately 98 percent of cotton is setting bolls compared with 95 percent last week. 15 percent is opening bolls which is slightly behind last year and the five year average. Insect pressure continues to be light but the arrival of the monsoon moisture increases the probability of more activity. ((Eileen Houlihan, New York Commodity Desk, 212-859-1640))
